mainEntity.name: Can I shoot my Airbnb listing on a phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — a modern smartphone (iPhone 12 or newer, or equivalent Android) on a tripod produces perfectly acceptable Airbnb photography for most listings. The tripod matters more than the camera. Phone wide-angle modes are usable but avoid the ultra-wide setting, which distorts corners.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time of day to photograph my holiday let?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bright-overcast days are the easiest to work with in the UK, because the light is soft and the windows aren't blown out. On sunny days, shoot each room when the sun is off its windows — late morning for west-facing rooms, mid-afternoon for east-facing rooms. North-facing rooms look good any time during daylight.

mainEntity.name: How many photos should I put in my Airbnb listing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Thirty to forty photos is the sweet spot for UK listings. Airbnb's algorithm rewards completeness, and guests want reassurance before they book. Cover every room and every feature — kitchen from two angles, bedrooms from two angles, bathrooms, exterior, outdoor space, and any unique features.

mainEntity.name: Should I use HDR for Airbnb photography?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not the heavy HDR look that's common in estate agent listings. Guests associate it with property sales and it often signals exaggeration. A very light HDR effect (minor shadow lift, minor highlight pull) in a single frame is fine — a fully processed HDR composite is not.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a wide-angle lens?

acceptedAnswer.text: A wide-angle lens or wide mode helps significantly with small UK rooms, but stay in the 16–24mm range on full frame (10–16mm on APS-C). Anything wider creates visible distortion that makes the listing look misleading — and misleading photographs lead to bad reviews.

mainEntity.name: How high should the camera be when shooting an Airbnb listing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chair height — around 1.2 to 1.4 metres from the floor. Eye-height shots (1.6m+) look down into rooms and make ceilings feel low. Chair-height shots feel balanced and give equal weight to floor and ceiling.

mainEntity.name: Can I photograph my Airbnb with guests staying there?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if the listing is empty of personal belongings. In practice this means photographing between bookings, during a deep clean, or on a dedicated changeover day. A rushed shoot over a guest's things will produce photos that look lived-in in the wrong way.

mainEntity.name: When is it worth hiring a professional instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you've recently refurbished, when your listing is competing in a crowded market (central London, the Cotswolds, Edinburgh), or when you run multiple properties. A professional shoot of 30 images is typically £300–£600 and the booking-rate uplift often pays it back inside one season.
